label: Tab Router
Turn on routing *Moves tabs into tab groups automatically as you browse, using the rules below. Nothing moves until you write at least one rule.*

Sort into *Tab groups are flat and never pinned. Zen folders nest, but gZenFolders.createFolder calls gBrowser.pinTab on every tab it is given and places the folder inside the pinned container -- there is no option to avoid that, so folders always pin their contents. Groups is the default for that reason. With groups, a rule named Google / Docs simply becomes a group with that name rather than a real subfolder.

Subfolder separator *Splits a rule's group name into folder levels. With the default, Work / Email / Gmail creates three levels deep. Only used when sorting into Zen folders. Include the spaces if you want them.'/' with no spaces works too.'*

Try to unpin tabs placed in folders *Zen folders live in the pinned area, so tabs filed into one arrive pinned. This tries two things: setting the folder itself to unpinned, and unpinning the tab. Neither is documented. Run TabRouter.testUnpin() in the console FIRST -- it runs the experiment on a single tab and tells you plainly whether the tab stayed in the folder or was ejected. Only turn this on if it says the tab stayed.*

Rules *One per line, or separated by semicolons. Left of the > is a comma separated list of domains, right of it is the group name. Subdomains match automatically, so github.com also catches gist.github.com. First match wins, so put narrower rules first. You do not have to write these by hand: open the Browser Console and run TabRouter.suggestRules() to generate a block from the tabs you already have open, or TabRouter.suggestRules({subdomains:true}) to get a nested Parent / Child rule per subdomain. It copies to your clipboard and moves nothing.*

Sort everything automatically *Derives the folder name from the site itself, so a page from somewhere you have never been still gets filed without any rule existing for it. Rules still win where they match, so use them to override the automatic name. This is the switch that makes the mod work with no setup.*

Use subdomains as subfolders *docs.proton.me becomes Proton / Docs rather than just Proton. www is ignored, since it is noise rather than a real subdomain. Only meaningful when sorting into Zen folders; with tab groups the whole path becomes one flat name.*
How many subdomain levels *How deep to nest for hosts like a.b.example.com. One level gives Example / B. Two gives Example / B / A. Most sites never need more than one.*

Use URL path as subfolders *Subdomains cannot split a site that separates sections by path. nexusmods.com/games/cyberpunk2077 has NO subdomain -- www is stripped -- so every game lands in one folder no matter how deep subdomain nesting goes. This reads path segments instead. One level on that URL gives Nexusmods / Cyberpunk2077, since 'games' is filtered as a generic word.*
Path words to ignore *Comma separated. Generic route words that would make useless folder names. Numeric segments and anything ending in a file extension are always dropped.*

Path name aliases *slug = Pretty Name, one per line or comma separated. A slug like baldursgate3 has no word boundaries, so no amount of cleverness recovers Baldur's Gate 3 from it -- that needs either a dictionary or the page title. Run TabRouter.suggestAliases() in the console: it reads your open tabs, pulls the human name out of each page title, and copies a ready-made list to your clipboard. Slugs that DO have separators, like crimson-desert or crimsonDesert, are cleaned up automatically and need no alias.*
Create groups that do not exist yet *Off means tabs are only moved into groups you already made by hand, and rules naming a missing group do nothing.*
Leave alone
Tabs already in a group *The important one. On, routing only ever touches loose tabs, so anything you filed by hand stays put. Turn it off only if you want rules to override your own sorting.*

Re-file tabs that drifted *A link opened from a grouped tab inherits that group even when it goes somewhere unrelated, which is why a stray domain stays stuck in the group it was opened from. With this on, a tab whose group no longer matches where it belongs gets moved. Only applies when tabs already in a group are otherwise skipped.*
Essentials *Essentials are pinned deliberately and are not loose tabs.*
Pinned tabs *Separate from Essentials.*
Timing
Sort everything at startup *Runs one pass a few seconds after the window opens. Off by default, since a session restore moving dozens of tabs at once is jarring.*

Wait before routing (milliseconds) *How long to wait after a page loads before moving its tab. A short delay avoids chasing redirects, which would otherwise file a tab under the redirector instead of the destination.*
Troubleshooting

Log what it is doing *Prints to the Browser Console (Ctrl+Shift+J) under [TabRouter]. Also gives you TabRouter.preview(), which lists every tab with the group it would go to without moving anything, and TabRouter.sortAll() to run one pass on demand.*
